questions.question: Discuss the role of energy input and scan speed in controlling microstructure during Directed Energy Deposition.
questions.solution_html:
• microstructureduring Directed Energy Deposition.
  • Energy Input (Laser/Beam Power)
  •  Higher energy → deeper melt pool → slower cooling → coarser
  • grains
  •  Lower energy → rapid solidification → finer microstructure
  •  Excess energy may cause porosity or distortion
  • Scan Speed
  •  High scan speed → less heat input → fine grains, higher
  • hardness
  •  Low scan speed → more heat accumulation → coarse grains
  • Combined Effect
  •  Determines cooling rate, grain size, and phase formation
  •  Proper balance ensures desired mechanical properties
questions.final_answer:  Proper balance ensures desired mechanical properties
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define topology optimization.
questions.solution_html:
• Topology Optimization is a computational design method that
  •  Optimizes material layout within a given design space
  •  Based on loads, constraints, and boundary conditions
  • Objective: Maximize performance while minimizing material usage
  • Widely used in lightweight and efficient structures
questions.final_answer: Widely used in lightweight and efficient structures
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Relate material properties to functional performance in AM components.
questions.solution_html:
• Relate material properties to functional performance in AM components.
  •  Strength & stiffness → Determines load-bearing capacity
  •  Thermal resistance → Important for high-temperature
  • applications
  •  Density → Affects weight and efficiency (e.g., aerospace parts)
  •  Surface finish → Influences friction, wear, and aesthetics
  •  Anisotropy (layer-wise properties) → Affects strength in different
  • directions
  •  Fatigue resistance → Important for cyclic loading conditions
  • Proper material selection ensures performance, durability, and reliability
  • of AM components.

questions.question: Design a 3D printed component while justifying choices related to wall thickness,infill density,and support structures.
questions.solution_html:
• Design a 3D printed component while justifying choices related to
  • wallthickness,infill density,and support structures.
  • When designing a component
  • (a) Wall Thickness
  •  Must be thick enough for strength but not excessive
  •  Thin walls → lightweight but may break
  •  Thick walls → stronger but increases material and print time
  •  Chosen based on load and material type
  • (b) Infill Density
  •  Low infill (10–30%) → lightweight, faster printing
  •  High infill (50–100%) → stronger, more durable
  •  Select based on functional requirement (strength vs weight)
  • (c) Support Structures
  •  Required for overhangs and complex geometries
  •  Ensures proper shape during printing
  •  Should be minimized to reduce material use and post
  • processing
